{{Quote|<nowiki></nowiki>''Beskar'' is a uniquely resistant iron that develops a wide range of properties—and colors—in the hands of skilled metalsmiths. Depending on the alloy, it can take any form from plate, laminate, and wire to foam, mesh, micronized particles, and even a transparent film. Mandalorians jealously guard their ''beskar''-working skills and refuse to sell the formulas for any price; attempts to reproduce finished ''beskar'' elsewhere have been disappointing. The ore is found solely on Mandalore, and only Mandalorians know how to work it to maximize its extraordinary properties.|Pilas Manaitis's ''Strategic Resources of the Galaxy''|<ref name="ImpCom501st">''[[Imperial Commando: 501st]]''</ref>}}
'''Mandalorian iron''', also known by its [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']] name of '''''beskar''''', was an extremely durable [[Iron/Legends|iron]] [[Ore/Legends|ore]] whose only known source was the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]] and its [[Moon/Legends|moon]], [[Concordia/Legends|Concordia]]. The [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Soldier/Legends|warrior]] culture that inhabited Mandalore [[Mining/Legends|mined]] their planet for ''beskar'', using it in the creation of weapons, [[Armor/Legends|armor]], and [[Starship/Legends|starships]], occasionally even [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|selling]] the rare and valuable metal on the [[Galactic economy|galactic market]]. The introduction of certain additives during the smelting process served to increase the strength of the natural ore, and Mandalorian [[Metalsmith/Legends|metalsmiths]] guarded the secrets of forging ''beskar'' from outsiders, passing along the techniques from one generation of metallurgists to the next, strictly within the Mandalorian community. A versatile metal, Mandalorian iron could be melded into multiple alloys and forged into various configurations.

==Description==
{{Quote|By the Force! I thought a lightsaber could cut through anything. The walls are barely scratched. The only thing that can resist a lightsaber is&hellip;Mandalorian iron!|Exar Kun, regarding Freedon Nadd's tomb|audio=NaddsTombMandoIron-DLOTS.flac|<ref name="Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio)">[[Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio drama)|''Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith'' audio drama]]</ref>}}
[[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Iron/Legends|iron]] was rare throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], as the only known source for the [[Ore/Legends|ore]] was the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]]<ref name="Sacrifice" /> and its [[Orbit/Legends|orbiting]] [[Moon/Legends|moon]], [[Concordia/Legends|Concordia]],<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> both located at the heart of [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalorian space]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Some speculated that ''beskar'' could be found in the other worlds of the [[Mandalore system/Legends|Mandalore system]], as well.<ref name="TBHC">''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]''</ref> The Mandalorians referred to the iron by the name ''beskar'', and despite the word's origins in the [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']] [[Language/Legends|language]], it became common for even non-Mandalorians to refer to the element as such.<ref name="ImpCom501st" /><ref name="Revelation">''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]''</ref> [[Mining/Legends|Mined]] from beneath the surface of Mandalore and Concordia,<ref name="TBHC" /> Mandalorian iron was one of the toughest metals known to science. Cherished for its incredible strength and durability, ''beskar'' was notable for being able to withstand blows from even a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]],<ref name="Sacrifice" /> and was commonly thought to be nearly indestructible,<ref name="HotM">{{InsiderCite|80|The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors}}</ref> making ''beskar'' more prized than [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]] or [[Cortosis/Legends|cortosis]].<ref name="TMPaC">{{InsiderCite|86|The Mandalorians: People and Culture}}</ref>

The natural strength of ''beskar'' was amplified during the forging process, using techniques developed and closely guarded by Mandalorian [[Metalsmith/Legends|metalsmiths]],<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> many of whom would sooner [[Death/Legends|die]] than reveal their secrets to outsiders.<ref name="TBHC" /> In the foundry, [[Carbon/Legends|carbons]] were often added to the ore to create a molecular cage structure that allowed Mandalorian iron to be lighter than contemporary metals, while still retaining its incredible toughness.<ref name="TMPaC" /> Without the addition of carbon, ''beskar'' was significantly heavier.<ref name="O66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref> Repeated folding of Mandalorian iron during forging further enhanced its strength.<ref name="TMPaC" /> Mandalorian metalsmiths combined ''beskar'' ore with several other metals to create multiple alloys capable of being shaped into various configurations, and were also responsible for affecting the final [[Color/Legends|color]] of the finished ''beskar'' during the smelting process.<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> When two pieces of ''beskar'' were struck together, the resulting sound was heavy and dull, more solid in resonance than the high [[Tin/Legends|tinny]] frequency produced from striking durasteel.<ref name="TC">''[[Republic Commando: True Colors]]''</ref>

==Usage==
{{Quote|If you're worth that much, you can afford some better armor. Look at the state of you. All scrapes.''"<br />"''We ''Mando'' boys like to show we've been in action. Anyway, this is top-grade ''beskar''—full density, two percent ciridium, no fancy lamination or carbon-alloy.|Ny Vollen and Kal Skirata on the latter's Mandalorian armor|<ref name="O66" />}}
[[File:Crushgaunts-Insider80.jpg|thumb|left|200px|[[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Crushgaunt/Legends|crushgaunts]] made use of micronized ''beskar'' [[Iron/Legends|iron]].]]
A versatile metal capable of being combined into several alloys and molded into a number of forms,<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> ''beskar'' became a common material in Mandalorian craftsmanship.<ref name="HotM" /> Depending upon the composition of the alloy, Mandalorian iron could be rendered into solid plates, a laminate, wire, [[Mesh armor|mesh]], or micronized particles, even a foam, or a transparent film.<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> Though materials such as durasteel<ref name="TMPaC" /> and [[alum]]<ref name="Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref> were commonly used in the creation of [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|Mandalorian armor]], Mandalorian iron was considered the most desirable choice for a [[Soldier/Legends|soldier's]] [[Armor/Legends|armor]].<ref name="TMPaC" /> Armor forged of ''beskar'' could withstand blunt force, strikes from a lightsaber, and repeated [[Blaster/Legends|blasterfire]], though the force of the impact still transferred in part to the wearer.<ref name="Revelation" />

Mandalorian iron was also a common resource in the production of weapons:<ref name="HotM" /> traditional Mandalorian [[Sword/Legends|sabers]] known as ''[[Beskad/Legends|beskade]]'' were forged of Mandalorian iron, with the metal folded and struck repeated during the process to create the sturdy blades.<ref name="Sacrifice" /> Mandalorian [[Kal/Legends|''kal'']] [[Knife/Legends|knives]] were also cast from ''beskar'' iron.<ref name="TBHC" /> Micronized ''beskar'' was used in the creation of powerful [[Crushgaunt/Legends|crushgaunts]], capable of breaking [[Bone/Legends|bone]] with ease,<ref name="HotM" /> and bladed ''[[bes'bev]]'' [[Flute/Legends|flutes]] were crafted from Mandalorian iron, as well.<ref name="O66" /> ''Beskar'' could be employed in the creation of [[Lightsaber hilt/Legends|lightsaber hilts]] in order to make them capable of resisting blows from an opposing blade, and Mandalorian iron crafted into hand-held shields could be used for defense and offense alike, allowing the wielder to strike their opponent or cut them with edges that have been honed to a razor sharpness.<ref name="BoS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>

Ancient [[Mandalorian manacles]] were made of ''beskar'', and the tough Mandalorian iron allowed them to compete with the advent of newer [[Binders/Legends|binder]] technology, such as [[force shackles]] and [[Energy cuffs|laser cuffs]], for [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]].<ref name="HotM" /> Many buildings in the [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorian]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Sundari/Legends|Sundari]] utilized ''beskar'' in their construction, and Mandalorian iron was used in the creation of the city's [[Royal prison/Legends|prison]] cells,<ref name="ShadowConspiracy">''[[The Clone Wars: Darth Maul: Shadow Conspiracy]]''</ref> just as it had been for [[Standard year/Legends|years]] in powerful ''beskar'' [[cage]]s.<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> ''Beskar'' was also often used in the construction of Mandalorian [[Starship/Legends|starships]],<ref name="HotM" /> including the likes of the ''[[Bes'uliik]]''-class [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]], which featured an outer armored shell of micronized Mandalorian iron.<ref name="Sacrifice" />

==History==
===Early history===
{{Quote|Now that you have abundant ''beskar'', you'll rearm. Roche may be outside of your sector, but the last time Mandalorians had plenty of ''beskar'', the Mandalore sector became much, much bigger.|Sass Sikili|<ref name="Sacrifice" />}}
The ancient [[Taung/Legends|Taung]] progenitors of the Mandalorian culture were said to have been drawn to what became Mandalorian space by the lure of indestructible ''beskar'' ore,<ref name="TBHC" /> and discovered ''beskar'' sometime after their conquest of the planet Mandalore around [[7000 BBY]].<ref name="TEA" /> The acquisition and use of Mandalorian iron was a contributing factor in the early expansion of the Mandalore sector.<ref name="Sacrifice" /> Mandalorian metalsmiths developed techniques and different methods for working the iron which they came to guard closely from outsiders, and passed down from one generation to the next.<ref name="HotM" /> However, its incredible strength attracted the attention of many non-Mandalorians, and ''beskar'' quickly earned a reputation as one of the strongest metals known to science, and one of the most desirable elements in the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]; [[Army/Legends|armies]] throughout the galaxy sought to obtain supplies of Mandalorian iron, and it became one of the most valuable metals on the [[Galactic economy|galactic market]].<ref name="Sacrifice" /> Attempts to purchase the knowledge of ''beskar'' iron-working from Mandalorian metalsmiths though the years had all failed, and all endeavors to replicate finished ''beskar'' without the aid of Mandalorian craftsmen had been met with similarly poor results.<ref name="ImpCom501st" />

Mandalorians furnished starships and constructed weapons with ''beskar'',<ref name="HotM" /> while the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Arca Jeth]] utilized a heavy slab of Mandalorian iron to seal the [[Tomb of Freedon Nadd|tomb]] of the deceased [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Freedon Nadd]] on [[Dxun/Legends|Dxun]]. The ''beskar'' door proved an impediment for the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]], who was shocked to find that his lightsaber was rebuffed by the Mandalorian iron, and only gained access to the blocked [[Burial/Legends|tomb]] with repeated strikes of his saber at its highest power output.<ref name="TOTJ">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 2|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 2]]</ref> By the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]], Mandalorians had come to view ''beskar'' as the ideal material for crafting Mandalorian armor, and recognized the substantial benefits it provided when battling lightsaber-armed [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force wielders]],<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> a viewpoint that lasted for generations.<ref name="TMPaC" /> The [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Darth Rivan]] also made use of Mandalorian iron in his [[Almas Sith fortress|Sith fortress]] on [[Almas]]: the door to his ritual chamber and the floor of his lightsaber practice room were crafted from ''beskar'', as was a chest Rivan used to hold his most valued Sith tomes.<ref name="AMA">{{LivingForce|A Mon Alone}}</ref> Another Sith, Lord [[Odion]] of the [[Grumani sector/Legends|Grumani sector]], had a throne of Mandalorian iron installed aboard the [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]] of his [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], the [[Sword of Ieldis (starship)|''Sword of Ieldis'']],<ref name="KnightErrant">[[Knight Errant (novel)|''Knight Errant'']]</ref> while some [[Sith Warrior|Sith warriors]] elected to wear heavy [[Beskar'kandar|''beskar'' armor]] as part of their [[Sith apparel|apparel]].<ref name="BoS" />

===A Mandalorian resource===
{{Quote|<nowiki></nowiki>''Beskar'' is enormously strong, able to deflect blaster bolts and even lightsaber blades. Yet it is light and flexible, particularly when forged with carbon and ciridium. A skilled ''naur'alor'' can shape ''beskar'' into almost any form, manipulating its strength, color, and other properties. This knowledge is ours alone...|Tor Vizsla, founder and leader of the Death Watch|<ref name="TBHC" />}}
[[File:ConcordianMines-Overview.png|thumb|right|300px|[[Concordia/Legends|Concordia]], one of Mandalore's moons, was extensively mined for Mandalorian iron ore]]
As time went on, Mandalorian iron became a prominent export from the planet Mandalore, fulfilling an economic niche for the Mandalorians on the galactic market.<ref name="Sacrifice" /> Following the [[Mandalorian Excision]] of [[738 BBY]] that birthed the peaceful [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorian]] faction,<ref name="TEGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> the pacifist sect made substantial use of Mandalorian iron in the construction of their capital city of Sundari, located in one of the [[white]]-sand [[Desert/Legends|deserts]] of Mandalore. Many of the city's grand buildings and towers featured ''beskar'' in their architectural makeup, and durable Mandalorian iron was used in the creation of cells at the city's [[Prison/Legends|prison]].<ref name="ShadowConspiracy" /> Some of the ''beskar'' utilized by the New Mandalorians came from breaking down suits of traditional Mandalorian armor the pacifist sect had relinquished upon embracing peace, repurposing the material toward non-martial ends.<ref name="TBHC" />

Before the Mandalorians ceased waging large-scale warfare,<ref name="TMP">{{TCW|The Mandalore Plot}}</ref> they turned to Mandalore's moon, Concordia, seeking to uncover new deposits of ''beskar'' ore.<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> Once an [[Agriworld/Legends|agricultural]] settlement, Concordia was transformed into a mining base<ref name="TMP" /> by Mandalorian prospectors who scoured the moon for ''beskar''. Ugly [[Concordian mines/Legends|mines]] came to scar the surface of Concordia,<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> and the mining operation was so extensive that the [[Tree/Legends|forests]] of Mandalore's moon were nearly destroyed in the effort. The mining operations on Concordia eventually slowed, to the point they were believed by the New Mandalorian government to have ceased altogether.<ref name="TMP" /> However, the forces of the [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]]—a violent and radical Mandalorian splinter group that opposed both the modern [[Supercommando Codex|honorable ways]] of the warrior clans<ref name="HotM" /> and the pacifism of the New Mandalorians—continued to maintain mining operations on Mandalore and Concordia in secret, acquiring ''beskar'' for weapons and armor. The Death Watch's founder and [[Secret Mandalore|leader]], [[Tor Vizsla]], touched upon these mining efforts and ''beskar'' in general in a manifesto he wrote entitled ''[[Ba'jurne Kyr'tsad Mando'ad]]''.<ref name="TBHC" />

[[Mandalorian Guard/Legends|Mandalorian police]] units continued to make use of ancient ''beskar''-forged Mandalorian manacles during this time, keeping them as part of their standard equipment,<ref name="HotM" /> as well as blastproof ''beskar'' shields.<ref name="TBHC" /> The personal star [[Yacht/Legends|yacht]] of the New Mandalorian [[Anti-Mandalore|leader]], [[Duchess/Legends|Duchess]] [[Satine Kryze/Legends|Satine Kryze]], was furnished with ''beskar'' flatware used by passengers for dining.<ref name="NewBattlefronts" />

[[File:Kal_Skirata_by_Brian_Rood.jpg|thumb|left|200px|[[Kal Skirata]]'s [[Gold/Legends|gold]]-[[Color/Legends|colored]], ''beskar''-forged [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|Mandalorian armor]]]]
By the start of the galaxy-spanning [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the effects of the widescale ''beskar'' mining operation on Concordia began to fade, and the moon's forests had begun to flourish again.<ref name="TMP" /> At this time, the Mandalorian soldier [[Walon Vau]] possessed black ''beskar''-forged Mandalorian armor in addition to a traditional Mandalorian ''beskad'' saber.<ref name="TZ">''[[Republic Commando: Triple Zero]]''</ref> [[Wad'e Tay'haai]], Vau's [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] contemporary and a fellow Mandalorian member of the ''[[Cuy'val Dar]]''—an elite group of training [[Sergeant/Legends|sergeants]] [[Limb/Legends|hand]]-picked to instruct the [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commandos]] of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]]—owned a bladed Mandalorian ''bes'bev'' flute cast from Mandalorian iron, painted the same violet color as his iron armor. Tay'haai's good friend, and another member of the ''Cuy'val Dar'' by the name of [[Kal Skirata]], wore armor that was a Mandalorian iron alloy containing two percent [[ciridium]]. Skirata's armor lacked carbon in its composition,<ref name="O66" /> traditionally used to form a molecular cage structure that made ''beskar'' lighter,<ref name="TMPaC" /> resulting in a significant weight increase.<ref name="O66" /> Around this time, [[Pilas Manaitis]] wrote at length on the attributes and advantages of Mandalorian iron in his work ''[[Strategic Resources of the Galaxy]]''.<ref name="ImpCom501st" />

After the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] was [[Declaration of a New Order|transformed]] into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], Imperials began brokering negotiations with the clan [[Chief/Legends|chieftains]] of Mandalore in order to establish a [[Garrison/Legends|garrison]] [[City of Bone|base]] on the planet and acquire the rights to mine for Mandalorian iron. An offer of eight hundred million [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] was issued for exclusive ''beskar'' mining rights in the verdant [[Tokursh]] region of Mandalore, and the [[MandalMotors/Legends|MandalMotors]] company was solicited to refurbish old [[Mandalorian dungeon ship|prison ships]] and construct [[Lictor-class dungeon ship|new ones]] with Mandalorian iron enhancements. In addition, requests were made to acquire specialist ''beskar'' equipment including manacles, holding cages, and security doors.<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> However, as time passed, relations between the Empire and Mandalore changed from cordial to hostile: Mandalore was taken over by the Imperials and its people [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]].<ref name="GaW">''[[Galaxy at War]]''</ref> The Empire strip-mined Mandalore's shallow veins of ''beskar'' ore, shipping a significant amount offworld<ref name="Sacrifice" /> before [[Fenn Shysa]] and the [[Mandalorian Protectors (Spar)|Mandalorian Protectors]] were able to liberate Mandalore from the Empire.<ref name="GaW" /> Around this same time, the [[Lumiya's Sith|Sith Lady]] [[Lumiya]] used Mandalorian iron to construct portions of [[Lumiya's lightwhip|her lightwhip]].<ref name="Lumiya">{{DB|character|lumiya|Lumiya}}</ref>

In [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]], at the four-hundred-twelfth [[Proceedings of Galactic Anthropology and History]] at the [[Brentaal Academy]] on [[Brentaal IV/Legends|Brentaal IV]], [[Historian/Legends|historian]] [[Vilnau Teupt]] gave a keynote speech entitled "[[Industry, Honor, Savagery: Shaping the Mandalorian Soul]]." During the speech, he discussed the place of ''beskar'' in the vast history and culture of the Mandalorian people.<ref name="TEGW" />

===War and resurgence===
{{Quote|<nowiki></nowiki>''Mand'alor'', you're looking at a test forging from a new lode of ''beskar."<br />"''But the Empire strip-mined Mandalore. They took all the iron.''"<br />"''They missed a bit. A ''big'' bit. ''[...]'' This is a planet with a tiny population, and even the Imperials didn't survey all of it. They stripped the shallow veins. This is a deeper lode, and we'd never have found it if the ''vongese'' hadn't left craters you could sink a small moon in. There's a crew a hundred klicks north of Enceri still doing test drills, but it looks like a big, ''big'' lode that was exposed.|Medrit Vasur and ''Mand'alor'' Boba Fett, discussing the discovery a new lode of ''beskar'' ore on Mandalore|<ref name="Sacrifice" />}}
[[File:Beskad-BHC.png|thumb|right|250px|[[Goran Beviin]] wielded a deadly ''beskar''-forged Mandalorian saber known as a ''[[Beskad/Legends|beskad]]'' in battle]]
[[Standard decade/Legends|Decades]] later, the Mandalorian soldier [[Goran Beviin]] came to possess an antique ''beskad'' forged of Mandalorian iron, as well as a pair of micronized ''beskar''-laden crushgaunts. When the [[Yuuzhan Vong galaxy|extra-galactic]] [[Species/Legends|race]] of invaders known as [[Yuuzhan Vong]] launched an [[Yuuzhan Vong War|attack]] on the known galaxy with the intent to conquer it, Beviin battled the aliens with both iron-made weapons.<ref name="APM">''[[Boba Fett: A Practical Man]]''</ref> After the end of the galactic invasion by the Yuuzhan Vong and their devastating [[Battle of Mandalore (Yuuzhan Vong War)|attack]] on Mandalore, a new source of Mandalorian iron was discovered in [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]]. Heeding the orders of reigning [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], two Mandalorians—one a [[Geologist/Legends|geologist]], and the other a [[minerals engineer]]—were returning to Mandalore when they decided to take an orbital scan of the surface damage that had been incurred by the Yuuzhan Vong. Upon comparing their results to previous geographic data, the two elected to investigate further upon planetary approach, only to find an undiscovered lode of ''beskar'' a few [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] north of the small town of [[Enceri]]. The iron had been deeper than the Imperials thought to mine during their occupation, exposed by chance by a Yuuzhan Vong [[Singularity mine|singularity bomb]]. [[Foreman/Legends|Foreman]] [[Herik Vorad]] was placed in charge of overseeing the mining of the new ''beskar'' lode, and as it was found on land that didn't belong to any one individual, ''Mand'alor'' Fett declared the iron to be a resource for all of Mandalore. He also settled on a compromise that allocated a portion of the Mandalorian iron to be manufactured into goods for foreign export, while another portion would be kept for the Mandalorians' domestic needs, including defense armament.<ref name="Sacrifice" />

This new lode of Mandalorian iron led to an economically prosperous era for Mandalore, and the creation of new starships such as the ''Bes'uliik''-class starfighter by MandalMotors—whose [[Chief Executive Officer/Legends|CEO]], [[Jir Yomaget]], elected to provide the ''Bes'uliik'' line with micronized ''beskar'' armor instead of a ''beskar'' laminate<ref name="Sacrifice" />—and the [[Tra'kad-class transport|''Tra'kad'']], which employed heavy Mandalorian iron armor plating.<ref name="Revelation" /> In [[41 ABY]], Goran Beviin and [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] Knight [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]] used ''beskar'' training armor and ''beskad'' sabers during sparring sessions, while Beviin attempted to teach Solo Mandalorian fighting techniques in order to better combat her Sith Lord brother, [[Darth Caedus]]. Around the same time, Beviin's [[Marriage/Legends|husband]] [[Medrit Vasur]] forged a set of ''beskar'' Mandalorian armor for Boba Fett to replace his old set comprised of durasteel plates. Fett put his new plates to good use soon after, during the [[Second Battle of Fondor]], where his Mandalorian iron armor blocked incoming blasterfire while he and over a dozen [[Mandalorian Supercommando|Mandalorian supercommandos]] assaulted the [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] [[Bloodfin (Star Destroyer)|''Bloodfin'']]. When the battle was over and ''Bloodfin'' had been captured by the Mandalorians, Fett met with Imperial [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Natasi Daala]], who revealed that she knew where much of the Mandalorian iron the Empire had stolen from Mandalore was located, and suggested the possibility of having it returned to the Mandalorians.<ref name="Revelation" /> Upon completing her training under Beviin, Jaina Solo was furnished with ''beskar'' armor plates, which she used during her decisive [[Battle of Uroro Station|clash]] with Darth Caedus aboard the [[Anakin Solo (starship)|''Anakin Solo'']]. Solo also learned from her uncle, [[Grand Master/Legends|Jedi Grand Master]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], how to perceive the faint flaws left in ''beskar'' during the forging process and use the Force to [[Shatterpoint/Legends|shatter]]<ref name="Invincible">''[[Legacy of the Force: Invincible]]''</ref> the otherwise impervious Mandalorian iron<ref name="TBHC" /> by exploiting those imperfections.<ref name="Invincible" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|<nowiki></nowiki>''Beskar'' is another name for Mandalorian iron, a super-strong Star Wars metal. Mandalorian armor is tough enough to withstand lightsaber strikes.|Daniel Wallace|<ref name="BoS Notes">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2012/03/endnotes-for-star-wars-book-of-sith_30.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: Book of Sith (part 3)|date=2012-09-03}}</ref>}}
Though Mandalorian manacles had first appeared in [[Tales of the Jedi 5|''Tales of the Jedi'' 5]], it was only in the later [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith|''Dark Lords of the Sith'' arc]] of the [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi (comic series)|''Tales of the Jedi'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] series that Mandalorian iron was truly introduced to ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]]. The same story was also responsible for introducing Mandalorian iron's lightsaber resistant capabilities.<ref name="TOTJ" /> With the release of the ''[[Republic Commando]]'' novel series<ref name="TC" /> and the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' article, ''[[The Mandalorians: People and Culture]]'', each [[Author/Legends|authored]] by [[Karen Traviss]], Mandalorian iron was given the additional ''Mando'a'' name of ''beskar'',<ref name="TMPaC" /> which has been used increasingly in more recent sources.<ref name="TOR" /><ref name="TBHC" /><ref name="TEGW" /> The ''People and Culture'' article, in addition to the previous ''Insider'' article, [[The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors|''The History of the Mandalorians'']] by [[Abel G. Peña]], provided details on the use, composition, and cultural significance of Mandalorian iron.<ref name="HotM" /><ref name="TMPaC" /> In [[2013]], the reference guide ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]'', co-written by [[Jason Fry]], [[Daniel Wallace]], and [[Ryder Windham]], featured a section and several informational references pertaining to Mandalorian iron.<ref name="TBHC" />
